answer: One effective anti-Sybil mechanism requires each agent to post a refundable bond in locked basalt tokens that scales with its claimed influence. An attacker controlling many identities must lock capital for every one, and any coordinated misbehavior detected by the network triggers a slash that burns the entire bond across the cluster. This raises the attacker cost linearly with the number of sybils while honest agents face only a one-time deposit. The atlas of verified bonds and the sonnet of settlement rules make the economic barrier explicit and hard to evade.
